content: Virkon is a commercially available, highly effective, multi-purpose disinfectant. It is widely utilized in various settings, including hospitals, laboratories, nursing homes, funeral homes, medical and dental clinics, veterinary facilities, and other environments where pathogen control is essential. Its applications include cleaning hazardous spills, disinfecting surfaces, and soaking equipment. Virkon exhibits a broad spectrum of antimicrobial activity, effectively targeting viruses, fungi, bacterial spores, and bacteria, including mycobacteria such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It has also been proven effective against pathogens like SARS and avian influenza. For optimal efficacy, the solution must be generously applied to a surface and allowed to remain undisturbed for a minimum of two minutes, and up to ten minutes, before being wiped off. The disinfectant contains several active and auxiliary components, including potassium peroxymonosulfate (5%) as the primary disinfecting and cleaning agent, sodium hexametaphosphate as a buffering agent, Amaranth dye as a color indicator, and lemon extract as a masking odorant. These components work synergistically to enhance its pathogen-killing capabilities. Virkon is most commonly sold in the form of pink tablets or powder, which dissolve readily in water at concentrations typically ranging from 10 to 30 grams per liter. The pink coloration serves as a visual indicator to help gauge the solution's concentration during preparation. Over time, the solution's color fades, signaling when it needs to be replaced. Once prepared, the solution remains stable for approximately five to seven days. The product has a faint lemon scent, though some users may still find the odor unpleasant. While it is relatively safe for skin contact, it can cause significant eye irritation and should not be used as a hand-washing liquid. When purchased in bulk, Virkon costs approximately 35 US cents per liter to produce, making it comparable in price to most bleach-based disinfectants. However, some facilities opt to create their own alternative disinfectants to reduce costs. Virkon is a registered trademark of Antec International, a subsidiary of DuPont. Since 2006, DuPont has been gradually rebranding Virkon as part of its RelyOn disinfectant product line.
